name: Cairo Road and the CBD
description: The wide central artery the city grew along, with the banks, the bus stations and the markets around it. It is congested, busy and functional, and it is where the practical business of Lusaka happens rather than where anyone chooses to live.
bestFor: Anyone needing banks, ministries or long-distance buses
pros: Bus stations for the whole country

name: Kabulonga
description: The most desirable residential district, southeast of the centre, with large houses behind walls, mature gardens, international schools and the shopping centres that serve them. Most of Lusaka's diplomatic and professional population lives here.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting security, space and international schools
pros: Safest and greenest part of Lusaka
cons: The most expensive area in the city

name: Rhodes Park and Longacres
tagline: Between the centre and the suburbs
description: Central residential districts with embassies, guesthouses, offices and a mix of older houses and newer apartment blocks. They sit close enough to the centre to be practical and far enough out to be quiet, which is the compromise most people take.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a central position without Kabulonga prices
pros: Close to both the centre and the embassies
cons: Mixed in character block to block
Still needs a car for most errands

name: Woodlands and Ibex Hill
tagline: The southern and eastern edges, spacious and green
description: Low-density residential areas on the southern and eastern edges of the city, with large plots, more tree cover and a good deal of newer building. Lusaka National Park, which holds white rhino within half an hour of the capital, is out this way.
bestFor: Anyone wanting space, quiet and a garden with solar
pros: Room for solar and battery installations
cons: Twenty-five minutes or more from the centre

name: Northmead
description: A small commercial district northeast of the centre with a concentration of bars, restaurants and live music venues, plus a market and shops. It is where a lot of Lusaka's going out happens and is more walkable than most of the city.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the nightlife within walking distance
pros: The best concentration of bars and live music
More walkable than most of Lusaka
Market and shops on the doorstep
